item.title: Xavier v. Detroit Mercy: Preview, matchups, and keys to the game
item.description: Detroit Mercy Titans forward London Maiden (20) pushes past Wright State Raiders forward Michael Imariagbe (33) on Tuesday, March 10, 2026, at Corteva Coliseum at the Indiana State Fairgrounds in Indianapolis. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co There is a limited amount of information that can reliably be garnered from the amount of games played at this point in the season, and it’s questionable whether or not that information will be accurate or even pertinent when March rolls around. A lot can change during the course of a college basketball campaign, and both attrition and development will change the composition and performance of virtually every roster during that time. Those disclaimers should serve as context when I tell you that Detroit Mercy is not a good team and this game will serve only as a counting stat in the Q4 column when resume time rolls around. Fresh off of a season in which they won just a single non-conference game against D1 competition, UDM lost by 61 to Marquette in their season opener on Friday. They peaked at 1.2% win probability by trailing just 9-8 before surrendering a 10-0 run in just over two minutes of game time. A 36-5 run that straddled the half functionally ended the game, as 36-5 runs tend to do. Pick a stat and it looks bad for them, but maybe the most notable is that they scored in just 6 of their 34 second half possessions. It was a destruction. Xavier, on the other hand, has been gorging on cupcakes. The Muskies brushed aside Mount St. Mary’s in the opener and then outscored Eastern Michigan 65-35 after the second media timeout of the game to turn a slow start into a comfortable victory. Sterner tests lie ahead, but for the moment, X has been giving it to all takers while barely breaking a sweat. Team fingerprint As might be expected of a team that lost by 60, the numbers aren’t pretty for Detroit Mercy. They’re a merely bad offensive rebounding team; the rest of the offensive side of the ledger is absolutely abysmal. They’re in the bottom 10 of D1 in free throw rate, turnover rate, and EFG% as a team. They can’t hit from inside or beyond the arc, and they’re poor from the line. They had almost a quarter of their two-point shots blocked and played at a glacial pace. Just ugly ball. Defensively, it’s not as bad, but it’s still not good. They managed to keep Marquette off the line, though that appears to be through a lack of meaningful resistance rather than any real defensive nous. They somehow forced just 3 turnovers in a 67 possession game, which is honestly incredible. The rest of the numbers are also bad, but again, it’s a one game sample. I think the biggest takeaway is that Marquette destroyed them and, if Xavier wants to compete near the top of the Big East this year, they need to do the same. item.title: Boston Half winner Habtom Samuel withdraws from 2026 Manchester Road Race
item.description: A file photo of the Manchester Road Race. (Courtesy of Rick Dyer) MANCHESTER - Boston Half marathon winner Habtom Samuel announced Monday night that he will not be running in this year's Manchester Road Race due to fatigue. Samuel, who won the Boston Half marathon Nov. 8, had committed to running in the annual Thanksgiving Day race in Connecticut on Sept. 9, according to a news release from the Manchester Road Race Committee. Race officials announced his entry alongside a lineup of other elite athletes and former Manchester Road Race winners in a media release Monday. However, Samuel's manager informed the race in an email Monday night that Samuel was withdrawing from the race due to "fatigue from such a long competitive season," according to the race committee's release. "We are disappointed, but hopefully Habtom will compete in Manchester in the future," said Jim Harvey, the Manchester Road Race's elite runner coordinator. "We still have an exceptional elite field and it will be another great race this year." Harvey announced Monday that this year's race participants will include 2025 men's division winner Edwin Kurgat , 2025 runner-up Dave Mullarkey and World Champion Dawit Seare. They will be joined at the Main Street starting line by 2023 Manchester Road Race winner Morgan Beadlescomb and two-time Manchester Road Race champion and Olympic silver medalist Sally Kipyego. Presented by Hartford HealthCare and organized by more than 400 volunteers, the annual Manchester Road Race will be held Thanksgiving Day at 10 a.m. The race will be held on a 4.737-mile loop through the central streets of Manchester, starting and finishing on Main Street in front of St. James Church. Registration is available online for $40, and then will increase to $42 on Nov. 21. Participants unable to make it to Manchester on Thanksgiving Day can sign up for the race's virtual option, according to Danie Kennedy, registrar and executive board member of the Manchester Road Race Committee. Participants can register for the online option for $30 and download the race app to track their progress, Kennedy said. All registration will close at 11:59 p.m. Nov. 24, Kennedy said. Main Street will close at 5:30 a.m. the day of the race and remain closed until 11:30 a.m., according to the event's website. All roads intersecting the racecourse as well as exit ramps from Interstate 384 will be closed at 9 a.m., with normal traffic resuming after 11:30 a.m., the website said. All proceeds from this year's race will be split between Rebuilding Together of Manchester and Habitat for Humanity of North Central Connecticut . item.title: Australian Jockey Izzy Neale Dead at 22 After Being Thrown From Her Horse
item.description: Newscom/MEGA Australian apprentice jockey Izzy Neale has died after an incident that took place over the weekend in New South Wales. She was 22. Reuters reported on Tuesday, November 10, that she was thrown from her horse, Marnoo, during the Warren Shire Cotton Cup on Sunday, November 8, and airlifted to Dubbo hospital. “It is with deep sadness and broken hearts that we announce the passing of our beloved Izzy, surrounded by her closest family and friends,” read a statement from the family posted on the official Racing NSW X account . “Izzy rode horses before she could walk,” the statement continued. “Her love of horses was a lifelong passion that, more recently, had grown into a love of racing.” Noting that Izzy’s organs will be donated, the family said she will “give others the chance of life, bringing some comfort to our family amid this devastating loss.” The family thanked their relatives, friends and the racing community as well as Racing NSW, the NSW Jockeys Association and “the medical staff who cared for Izzy with such compassion” for their support. “As we come to terms with our loss, we ask that our family’s privacy be respected,” the statement concluded. “Izzy was dearly loved and will forever be in our hearts.” Newscom/MEGA According to the New York Post , Izzy “lost consciousness” after she was dislodged from her horse at about the 400-meter mark during the Warren Shire Cotton Cup. She was reportedly placed on life support after being taken to the hospital. Per the Post , the final race of the program was abandoned, and Marnoo was euthanized. Thoroughbred Daily News reported that jockey Diego Montes de Oca was also dislodged from his horse and suffered a foot injury. According to the outlet, Izzy’s death is the first racing fatality in New South Wales since Darren Jones died in April 2017. Izzy’s brother Tommy Neale wrote on Facebook that he couldn’t “believe what’s happened,” adding: “You’ll always be my lil baby sister, you were my best friend an we always was so close so I dunno how I’m gonna deal with this.” “I’m so sorry I spent years in jail and didn’t spend much time together before this accident,” he added. “I can’t even comprehend how I feel till we meet again sis ❤ gonna miss you so much!!” Read More From First for Sports Josh Allen Goes Viral for Avoiding Eye Contact With Attractive Female Reporter During Postgame Interview Tony Romo Returns to Football Commentary in Unexpected Appearance for First Time Since CBS Departure Arnold Schwarzenegger’s Son Makes Successful ‘Pro Debut’ in Natural Bodybuilding Competition This story Australian Jockey Izzy Neale Dead at 22 After Being Thrown From Her Horse first appeared on First for Sports . item.description: JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA - AUGUST 21: Joey Aguilar #17 of the Jacksonville Jaguars throws against the Carolina Panthers during the second half of the preseason game at EverBank Field on August 21, 2026 in Jacksonville, Florida. (Photo by Mike Carlson/Getty Images) | Getty Images What a difference a few short weeks make in the National Football League. Take a look at the Arizona Cardinals quarterback room in training camp: Jacoby Brissett, seasoned veteran Gardner Minshew, third-round rookie Carson Beck, and 2025 holdover Kedon Slovis. RELATED: VETERAN QB JOSH JOHNSON SIGNED Take that same position group and view it today: Beck. In the past two days, Cardinals GM Monti Ossenfort has signed journeyman and free agent Josh Johnson, and has now claimed Joey Aguilar off the practice squad of the Jacksonville Jaguars. Apparently, Cardinals fans will get what they have been asking for since the 31-7 beating the team took from the Seattle Seahawks in Week 2. Beck seems the likely starter after Minshew is feared to have suffered a torn UCL in his throwing arm. Minshew injured his arm before the half, but continued to play. Currently, he is undergoing tests, so we will see. Meanwhile, the Cardinals signed 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson to the QB room, and today have claimed QB Joey Aguilar off the practice squad of the Jacksonville Jaguars. Just last week, Arizona shipped off their starting quarterback, Brissett, to the Baltimore Ravens for a 2027 fourth-round draft pick plus a 2028 seventh-round selection. Along with Brissett, the Cardinals gave up a 2027 fifth-round pick. Brissett was benched because of poor play, and the fact that the offense was stagnant. Minshew orchestrated two late comebacks in the same game, a 33-30 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Two days later, Brissett was traded. Given the Minshew news, perhaps the Arizona front office moved a little too early on that decision. The Cardinals were already down to two signalcallers before the Minshew injury. So, on Monday, GM Monti Ossenfort signed Johnson, who entered the league in 2009 and is now on his 19th NFL team. He has multiple stints with the San Francisco 49ers, New York Jets, Cincinnati Bengals, and the Ravens. His last contract was with the Bengals on a one-year $1.5 million deal. He played for the Sacramento Mountain Lions of the second version of the UFL in 2012. He was also signed to play with the San Diego Fleet of the AAF in 2019, but that league folded before he saw any game time. He was also signed by the Los Angeles Wildcats of the XFL in 2020, but COVID hit and all games were cancelled. Ossenfort was seeking a young arm to become QB3. Aguilar fits that bill at age 25. Aguilar (6’-3”, 229 pounds) went undrafted this past April in the NFL Draft out of Tennessee. item.description: The Cincinnati Bengals entered Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline looking for ways to strengthen their defense, particularly at linebacker. After exploring several options, the organization appeared to find an opportunity with the Philadelphia Eagles, agreeing to acquire outside linebacker Arnold Ebiketie . item.title: Potential Rams trade target Brian Thomas Jr. will not be moved
item.description: (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images If the Los Angeles Rams want to fill their increasing large void at wide receiver, they’ll have to look somewhere other than Brian Thomas Jr. According to Jeremy Fowler of ESPN, the Jacksonville Jaguars are planning to keep Thomas, ending months of speculation that the former Pro Bowler could be on the move. The Jaguars plan to keep WR Brian Thomas Jr. through the trade deadline, per sources. They have relayed that to interested teams. Coming off multiple big trades Monday, Jacksonville plans to keep its roster intact, barring a surprise. pic.twitter.com/0QxdybXqaN — Jeremy Fowler (@JFowlerESPN) November 10, 2026 This isn’t especially surprising from the Jaguars’ perspective, considering they’ve made it clear they’re going all in on a Super Bowl run this year. In just over 24 hours, the Jaguars have acquired safety Jessie Bates III, and defensive linemen Davon Godchaux and Jordan Davis, sending out a mass quantity of draft picks to get those deals done (including a first, two seconds, a fifth and a sixth). Given that their general manager, James Gladstone, used to work in the Rams front office, their approach is not surprising. But it does leave the Rams with one fewer option if they decide to bolster the receiver room at the NFL trade deadline. Thomas isn’t as good as Puka Nacua, who’s now on injured reserve , nor Davante Adams, who’s missed several weeks already with a hamstring injury . Despite that and despite a disappointing last couple seasons compared to his rookie debut, he’s still a talented player with a combination of speed and skill Los Angeles simply doesn’t have right now. He wouldn’t have fixed all of the passing game’s issues, but certainly could have helped. With this news, the best receiver on the likely trade block is Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts . This season, playing for a bad Colts offense with an even worse quarterback in Daniel Jones, Downs has posted 33 receptions for 354 yards and one touchdown, all hovering just below his career averages in terms of raw numbers and per-game efficiency. He’s a slot receiver, having taken over 52% of his snaps there this season, the third-highest rate in the NFL. That’s not a bad thing for this Rams offense, though, and actually should fit in well alongside a (hopefully eventually) healthy Nacua and Adams. item.title: Breslow Won’t Lock In Story, Leaving Red Sox Shortstop Spot Open
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Red Sox chief baseball officer Craig Breslow refused to name Trevor Story the starting shortstop for next season during Monday’s meetings in Las Vegas. This lack of a firm commitment sends a clear signal to the fanbase that the 34-year-old veteran is not a guaranteed lock. Breslow told reporters that while the team holds “a ton of confidence in Trevor,” final decisions will happen privately between him and the player long before any public announcement, according to the Boston Globe . A sports hernia injury limited Story to 64 games last season, resulting in a .235 average and .621 OPS, which explains the hesitation. Since signing a six-year, $140 million deal before the 2022 season, Story has appeared in just 384 of a possible 810 games. The math simply does not add up for a player on the final year of such a massive contract. Looking at the Bench Options The team is now openly considering other paths to fix the shortstop position. Breslow admitted the organization must be “open-minded about ways to improve the team” after finishing the 2026 season with an 87-75 record. Attention is turning toward minor league standout Franklin Arias, who posted a .957 OPS over 117 games last season. Breslow noted that the club is currently focused on “figuring out his readiness [for the majors] and what the timeline looks like” for the 21-year-old. With Arias finishing the year at Triple-A Worcester, the door is wide open for a younger, healthier option to take the job. A Front Office in Flux Breslow is also trying to rebuild the leadership behind the scenes while making roster decisions. He stated that the “executive leadership circle is down not just bodies, but down really talented people” after losing key assistant GMs Paul Toboni and Taylor Smith, according to Over the Monster . The General Manager role has remained vacant since 2023, adding to the instability. This lack of depth makes finding the right personnel even harder as the team aims to win more games in 2027 than they did in 2026. The front office is prioritizing new hires to fill these gaps before the season begins. With 54 points, rookie Payton Tolle placed third in AL Rookie of the Year voting, indicating bright spots within the team’s rotation. After retaining most of last year’s roster, Breslow characterized the Sox as “opportunistic” in the trade and free agent market.

item.title: NY Mets Rumor Claims Former All-Star Drawing ‘Interest From Multiple Teams,’ But Trade May Be Wrong Move
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A new rumor claims New York Mets pitcher Kodai Senga is drawing a good bit of interest around MLB. However, trading him now may not be the right move for the club. Despite having the largest payroll in baseball (without deferrals) this past season, the Mets were the league’s biggest disappointment as they finished dead last in the NL East with a 74-88 record. Before an expected lockout takes hold on Dec. 1, the Mets will be one of the teams that will be aggressive in improving the roster before major payroll changes come in a new collective bargaining agreement. While Gold Glove winner Nolan McLean is a great anchor for their pitching staff, they need a lot of help on that part of the roster after trading seven arms before this season’s deadline, including opening day ace Freddy Peralta. Furthermore, after an underwhelming debut season in Queens, it is unclear if Devin Williams will get a second chance at being the team’s closer in 2027. That is why a new rumor may not be as good as it would have been a year ago. According to a new report from The Athletic’s Will Sammon, Ken Rosenthal, and Katie Woo, “New York Mets pitcher Kodai Senga is attracting trade interest from multiple teams, ” with the general manager meetings now underway in Las Vegas. New York Mets should hold on to Kodai Senga, for now Sep 14, 2026; New York City, New York, USA; New York Mets relief pitcher Kodai Senga (34) pitches against the Baltimore Orioles during the ninth inning at Citi Field. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images If this were a year ago, or even before this season’s MLB trade deadline, the Mets would have jumped at moving Senga. After a strong debut in 2023 that earned him All-Star honors, the Japanese import has struggled with staying healthy and his stuff in the three seasons since. That is why the team has been looking to move him for much of the last year. Unsurprisingly, they had few takers for him and the money left on his five-year, $75 million contract . Senga was awful for the first four months of last season and eventually was moved to the bullpen. However, due to an injury to Williams, he was given a shot as the Mets’ closer, and he was great. In August, he posted a 1.74 ERA with five saves in 10.1 innings. Although he struggled a bit in September, he still posted three more saves. If the Mets are unsure about Williams, moving one of the few bullpen arms who pitched well late in the season would be a risk. Especially since the team already needs to add, not subtract, this offseason. While moving the money left on his contract would be a good thing, they might be better off seeing how they fare in free agency over the next couple of weeks and revisit a trade after the lockout. item.title: Debutants Tayyab Arif, Arafat Minhas shine as Pakistan pile up 434 before reducing Sri Lanka to 114/3 in Rawalpindi Test
item.description: Pakistan strengthened their position in the opening Test against Sri Lanka with a commanding batting display on Day 2 in Rawalpindi, posting 434/9 before reducing the visitors to 114/3 at stumps. Saud Shakeel narrowly missed a century, while debutants Tayyab Arif and Arafat Minhas made valuable half-centuries to put the hosts in control of the contest. Pakistan resumed the day at 281/5 and added 153 runs before captain Babar Azam declared the innings at 434/9 in 106.3 overs. Sri Lanka, who had opted to bowl after winning the toss, struggled to make early inroads as Pakistan's middle and lower order continued to frustrate their bowling attack. The visitors lost three wickets in their reply, with Mohammad Abbas and debutant Saqib Khan making crucial breakthroughs. Sri Lanka finished the day at 114/3, trailing Pakistan by 320 runs, with Kamindu Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva unbeaten when bad light brought an early end to proceedings. Saud Shakeel misses century as Pakistan build commanding total Resuming on 57, Saud Shakeel continued his patient knock and combined with wicketkeeper-batter Ghazi Ghori to frustrate the Sri Lankan bowlers. The duo stitched together a valuable 96-run partnership for the sixth wicket, taking Pakistan past the 300-run mark. Ghori looked set for a maiden Test half-century but fell for 48 off 72 deliveries after edging Dilshan Madushanka to Pasindu Sooriyabandara at gully. His innings included two boundaries and provided Pakistan with an important contribution in the morning session. Shakeel continued to hold one end together and moved closer to his fifth Test century. However, Asitha Fernando ended his resistance at 93 off 199 balls, with nine boundaries, as Kusal Mendis completed the catch. The dismissal also gave Fernando his 100th Test wicket, marking a significant milestone for the Sri Lankan pacer. Debutants Tayyab Arif, Arafat Minhas shine as Pakistan declare at 434/9 Pakistan's batting effort was supported by some impressive contributions from their debutants. Tayyab Arif had earlier scored a quickfire 57 off 51 balls, while Arafat Minhas continued his promising start to international cricket with a half-century. Minhas scored 52 off 72 deliveries, striking nine boundaries and a six. His counter-attacking approach helped Pakistan maintain the momentum even after the departure of Shakeel. Mohammad Taha also contributed a valuable 51, while captain Babar Azam scored 50 off 58 balls. The duo's half-centuries ensured Pakistan had contributions throughout the batting order. After Lahiru Kumara dismissed Razaullah for 10, Pakistan declared their first innings at 434/9 in 106.3 overs. For Sri Lanka, Asitha Fernando and Dilshan Madushanka picked up three wickets apiece, while Lahiru Kumara, Milan Rathnayake and Sonal Dinusha claimed one wicket each. item.title: Gerard Martin acknowledges the pressure on Barcelona defenders: ‘Will always be under scrutiny’
item.description: Gerard Martin acknowledges the pressure on Barcelona defenders: ‘Will always be under scrutiny’ Speaking in an interview with Achraf Ben Ayad (h/t Mundo Deportivo ), Gerard Martin has opened up on the scrutiny that comes with playing in the Barcelona defensive line. The 24-year-old versatile defender has become a regular fixture in Hansi Flick’s side, but he understands that his position will come under examination whenever results do not go in the favour of the Blaugrana . Martin opens up on Atletico Madrid win Martin granted the interview after Barcelona’s 2-1 win over Atletico Madrid this past weekend , which came at an important moment for the team. After all, there had been some question marks over the Catalans’ style of play and ability to get positive results against big teams following losses to PSG and Real Madrid. Moreover, a defeat to Atletico Madrid on Sunday would have seen Barça give up the top spot in La Liga to Diego Simeone’s men. Happy with the performances. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) Discussing the significance of the result, Martin noted: “It was important to win to gain an advantage. We’re doing well. We’re also still at the beginning of the season and we have to keep improving.” “I see the team doing well; it’s true that with the two important matches we lost in a row, people started murmuring, but I’m calm because we’re doing things right,” he added, about the team’s performance. The defender also acknowledged that Barcelona had not started the Atletico match as they would have wanted, having conceded an early goal. However, he was pleased with the way the players responded and managed to turn the game around. “It is true that the other day we didn’t start the game very well, but then we knew how to correct and overcome it and in the end we ended up winning, which is the important thing,” he said. On the pressure and scrutiny Martin expressed his happiness over his growing involvement in the team under Flick. Atthe same time, he insisted that he understood that Barcelona’s style of football inevitably places considerable attention on the backline. “Good, very happy to be playing. I’m taking it quite naturally because I know that with our style of play, if there’s any doubt, the defence will always be under scrutiny,” he admitted. Aware of the scrutiny. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) “In my case, if the team isn’t having a good period, the position of the defender and the centre-back will be questioned.” Martin was also asked about Barcelona’s ambitions in the UEFA Champions League. While winning the competition remains a major objective, he stated that the squad does not see the idea of lifting the trophy as an ‘obsession’. “I don’t know if we’re obsessed or not, but we have to take it one step at a time. item.description: John Jones-Imagn Images Celtics send not-so-subtle message to Jaylen Brown with shootaround song choice appeared first on ClutchPoints . The Boston Celtics appeared to send a playful message to former star Jaylen Brown ahead of Tuesday night’s highly anticipated matchup against the Philadelphia 76ers , playing the song “Why Can’t We Be Friends?” during their morning shootaround. Chris Hine of The Philadelphia Inquirer shared the observation on X, formerly known as Twitter, as Boston prepares to face Brown for the first time since his departure. “The first song being played at Celtics shootaround this morning is ‘Why Can’t We Be Friends?’ Almost TOO on the nose.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) While the song choice may have been coincidental, its timing drew attention ahead of the Celtics’ visit to Philadelphia. The Celtics (8-2) will face the 76ers (9-2) on Tuesday at 8 p.m. ET on NBC, marking the first regular-season meeting between Brown and longtime teammate Jayson Tatum as opponents. Jaylen Brown, Jayson Tatum reunite after years of success with Celtics Brown spent nine seasons with Boston from 2016-17 through 2025-26, including eight alongside Tatum after the Celtics selected the latter with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2017 NBA Draft. Together, the duo helped establish Boston as a perennial Eastern Conference contender, reaching the conference finals six times and making two NBA Finals appearances. Their greatest accomplishment came during the 2023-24 season, when they led Boston to its record 18th NBA championship with a five-game series victory over the Dallas Mavericks . Brown earned NBA Finals MVP honors after averaging 20.8 points, 5.4 rebounds and 5.0 assists in the championship series. The pair also reached the 2022 NBA Finals, falling to the Golden State Warriors in six games. Now playing for separate Eastern Conference contenders, Brown and Tatum enter Tuesday’s matchup with their respective teams among the NBA’s early-season leaders. Philadelphia has won nine of its first 11 games, while Boston enters the contest riding a three-game winning streak following Sunday’s 117-97 victory over the Milwaukee Bucks. item.title: LPGA Tour Championship bubble watch includes 9 (!) 2026 Solheim Cup players
item.description: The Annika driven by Gainbridge at Pelican is the ultimate tournament within a tournament on the LPGA. There's much at stake for many in this week's 108-player field in Belleair, Florida. World No. 1 Nelly Korda returns to the LPGA after a two-month break looking to win her fourth title at Pelican and clinch the final point needed to qualify for the LPGA Hall of Fame. While Korda vies for rare air, much of the field is fighting for next year's status. The top 100 in the Race to CME Globe points standings are secure for next season, while the top 60 earn a place in the season-ending CME Group Tour Championship in Naples, Florida. This year's CME at Tiburon Golf Club will offer a purse of $11 million and a $4 million winner's check. Among those on the bubble for the CME are a host of 2026 Solheim Cup players, including Angel Yin, who missed a good portion of the season with a stomach ailment. Yin is currently 58th on the list. Other players from the U.S. team fighting for a spot include Lindy Duncan (74th), Andrea Lee (77th) and Megan Khang (105th). On the European side, 2025 Annika champion Linn Grant has her work cut out at 84th. Spanish bomber Julia Lopez Rameriz, who had a T-9 and T-11 on the Asia swing, moved up to 66th. Right behind her in 68th is Nanna Koertz Madsen (68th). Euro rookies Nastasia Nadaud and Mimi Rhodes are 86th and 104th, respectively. That's nine out of a possible 24 Solheim Cup players in danger of missing the year-end, no-cut event. Sitting on the bubble in 60th is LPGA veteran Jodi Ewart Shadoff. Robyn Choi moved down one position to 61st after a T-47 last week in Japan. Multiple major winners Ariya Jutanugarn (76th), Minjee Lee (79th), Jin Young Ko (93rd) and Lilia Vu (101st) are all well outside the cutoff. Only Ko and Vu are entered in The Annika field. Lee, a three-time major winner, finished last in Japan over the weekend. Perennially one of the best ball-strikers in the game, Lee ranks 139th in driving accuracy and 135th in greens in regulation. Her scoring average over the last six events is 74.78. Beth Ann Nichols is a senior writer for Golfweek covering the LPGA and all things women's golf. Follow her on X/Twitter (@GolfweekNichols). item.title: Troy Aikman jokes he needs money to try Justin Jefferson’s diamond chain
item.description: Credit: ESPN Troy Aikman probably wasn’t talking about his contract on Monday night, but given his circumstances at ESPN, it was hard not to hear it that way. With Buck quietly signing a long-term contract extension at ESPN in the spring, and Aikman left without what he considers to be a serious offer, their futures at the worldwide leader being on different tracks has become a well-documented source of tension in the Monday Night Football booth . For the most part, that tension has not reared its ugly head during the broadcast. But one moment during Monday night’s matchup between the Buffalo Bills and Minnesota Vikings caught viewers’ attention, given the two broadcasters’ differing contract situations. Shortly before the half, Minnesota wide receiver Justin Jefferson’s massive diamond chain became a topic of discussion on the broadcast. Troy Aikman telling Joe Buck “if someone would lend me some money” https://t.co/QYBPM6xvLv — Chris Law (@ChrisLaw) November 10, 2026 “I’m guessing that’s insured; I just cannot imagine wearing that on a football field,” Aikman said. “I can’t imagine wearing it period if I’m being honest. I may try… if somebody will lend me some money.” Viewers didn’t have to look far for a potential lender. Buck signed a six-year, $108 million extension to stay at ESPN, while Aikman is heading toward free agency with no certainty about where he’ll be working next season. Both broadcasters are well aware of the headlines their contracts have generated in recent months, and neither seemed eager to linger on the line. Buck let out an awkward chuckle, and Aikman followed his own joke with a brief “huh” before the broadcast moved on. Don’t feel bad for Aikman, however. He’s in the final season of a $90 million contract with ESPN. And if ESPN really does go forward with breaking up what has widely been considered the best booth in football, Aikman will have opportunities in football, whether in media or in a front office . item.title: Arrowhead Pride Midseason Awards 2026: Most Improved Player
item.description: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images There are eight games in the books — with nine more to go. The Kansas City Chiefs ’ 2026 season reaches its midpoint in Week 10. Because the team’s bye came so early in Week 5, we have decided to move our annual awards to midseason. Nine members of the Arrowhead Pride writing staff each had one vote for our seven midseason awards, so nine votes will be tallied for each award. In this post, we’ll reveal our most improved player to this point in the season. DB Chris Roland-Wallace VOTING: DB Chris Roland-Wallace (4), DE Felix Anudike-Uzomah (3), DE Ashton Gillotte (1), CB Nohl Williams (1) Defensive back Chris Roland-Wallace joined the Chiefs as a rookie free agent out of USC following the 2024 NFL draft. An impressive camp saw him succeed in his long-shot bid for the final roster, and he instantly became one of Kansas City’s best special teams players. He flashed on defense throughout his first two seasons, but Roland-Wallace’s versatility has been instrumental as the Chiefs have managed injuries throughout the secondary early on. He played mainly safety to start the year as Chamarri Conner worked his way back from a training camp knee injury. As a safety, Pro Football Focus has given him a grade of 72.2 , ranking 20th out of 100 grades for the position. His 77.6 coverage grade on their metric ranks sixth of the 100 safeties. Pro Football Focus also credits Roland-Wallace with 14 solo tackles in run defense or open-field situations. With much of his work coming in the slot, Roland-Wallace has surrendered a somewhat high 84.6% completion percentage. However, he has been outstanding at limiting the damage in the middle of the field. Over eight games, he has surrendered only 6.4 yards per completion. In two games since veteran L’Jarius Sneed was placed on the Reserve/Injured (IR) list with a chronic knee injury, Roland-Wallace has seen his defensive snap count rise above 70% each of the last two weeks. The results on the field suggest he probably shouldn’t give up the workload, even if Sneed eventually returns. Roland-Wallace may never be a star, but he plays multiple roles and should stretch out a decent career as at least a high-end backup. Kansas City could have an interesting decision on him after the season. Roland-Wallace is in the final year of the three-year rookie free agent contract he signed in 2024. He will qualify for restricted free agency (RFA) following the season. Over the Cap projects the minimum RFA tender to be $3.8 million for the 2027 offseason. Because Roland-Wallace went undrafted, he would not net the Chiefs any draft-pick compensation if he signed with a new team (although Kansas City would have the right to match any offer). It is not hard to imagine another team signing him to a contract that may be difficult for the Chiefs—always tight against the salary cap—to swallow. Don’t be surprised if one of the team’s first offseason moves is a modest extension for Roland-Wallace

item.description: Power Rankings: Where does your team rank after Decision Day? By J. Sam Jones What a year in MLS. A team set a new points record, Lionel Messi won the Golden Boot and big spenders like Toronto and Atlanta struggled. It was truly a year unlike any other. As always: The Power Rankings are voted on by, give or take, 15 people associated with MLSsoccer.com. The author does not decide the rankings, but he does get a little rush out of getting to move your team in particular down a few spots when the votes come in. WATCH: Every goal from Decision Day! 1. Nashville SC The new record holders for points in a season lost just three (3!) whole times this season. Three. We’re running out of nice things to say about Nashville SC , who enter the postseason as MLS Cup favorites, so we’ll make sure the Cristian Espinoza signing this offseason gets its flowers. Nashville’s front office saw a need, went out and grabbed what they hoped would be a surefire hit, and watched as Espinoza put up 4g/15a. Espinoza has now delivered a double-digit assist total in five straight MLS seasons. He’s three away from 100 assists in his MLS career. Maybe more teams will try Nashville’s cutting-edge “adding good MLS players at a position of need” strategy down the line? Anyway, beyond Espinoza and Nashville’s excellent attack, it’s worth pointing out again that they were indestructible defensively in 2026. Nashville allowed just 25 goals all season. Since MLS moved to a 34-game schedule in 2012, no team has allowed fewer goals. Did we mention they’re the MLS Cup favorites? Previous: 2-0 win at CIN | Next: 11/22 vs. TBD, Round One, Game 1 2. Vancouver Whitecaps FC The Whitecaps ' post-World Cup performance has felt like a small step backward, but only because they were absolutely dominant in the first half of the season. They still finished with 32 points over 20 games after the World Cup. Only St. Louis and Dallas picked up more points in the West. Even with a small drop-off, it’s worth noting that the underlying numbers still love the ‘Caps. Per American Soccer Analysis’ expected points metric, only 2019 LAFC , the 2014 Galaxy , and 2018 Atlanta United have had better underlyings over a full season since 2013. Their expected goal differential per game is the second-best of any team in that span. “Nearly 2019 LAFC” is a heckuva thing to be. They’re still the favorite in the West. Previous: 2-0 win at MTL | Next: 11/22 vs. TBD, Round One, Game 1 3. In the second half of the season, the Herons finished with fewer points than six other Eastern Conference teams. Now they have to deal with red-hot Columbus in Round One.
